newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sibneft delays 500 billion rouble bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Sibneft delays 500 billion rouble bond issue.

text.p: Russia's OAO Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sibneft) oil company said on Friday it was postponing indefinitely a planned 500 billion rouble two-year bond.
The decision was taken on Thursday at an extraordinary meeting of shareholders at Sibneft headquarters in the Siberian city of Omsk.

"All documents for the issue were worked out in line with the old legal framework, so some of them run counter to the new federal law on joint-stock companies," Sibneft spokesman Alexander Vikulov told Reuters from Omsk.
Vikulov declined to say which points in particular needed to be corrected.
Company officials had said previously that bonds with denominations of five, 25 and 50 million roubles paying fixed annual interest of 18 percent would be issued.
Bondholders would have had the option of swapping the bonds for crude.
"The bonds issue has not been crossed off the company's agenda. It is to be resolved, but it is still too early to talk of any concrete date," Vikulov said.
Sibneft is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years. Its main operating unit is Noyabrskneftegaz. --Dmitry Solovyov, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
